summary:
bash: cd /app && cat > /tmp/verify.sh <<'SH'
set -u
R=/app/active_users_report.json
U=/app/users.json
fail=0
chk(){ if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then echo "PASS: $1"; else echo "FAIL: $1 ($3)"; fail=1; fi; }

# 1. output is an array
jq -e 'type=="array"' $R >/dev/null 2>&1; chk "output is JSON array" $?

# 2. only active users (set equality of user_ids)
A=$(jq -c '[.[]|select(.status=="active")|.id]|sort' $U)
B=$(jq -c '[.[].user_id]|sort' $R)
[ "$A" = "$B" ]; chk "contains exactly the active users (346)" $? "expected $(jq '[.[]|select(.status=="active")]|length' $U) got $(jq 'length' $R)"

# 3. exact key set & order in every object
jq -e 'all(.[]; (keys_unsorted == ["user_id","username","email","last_login","role_count","primary_role"]))' $R >/dev/null; chk "every object has exactly the 6 required keys" $?

# 4. last_login format YYYY-MM-DD
jq -e 'all(.[]; (.last_login|type=="string") and (.last_login|test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$")))' $R >/dev/null; chk "last_login matches YYYY-MM-DD" $?

# 5. last_login value equals input prefix
jq -n --slurpfile u $U --slurpfile r $R '($u[0]|map({key:(.id|tostring),value:.last_login[0:10]})|from_entries) as $m | all($r[0][]; .last_login == $m[(.user_id|tostring)])' | grep -q true; chk "last_login equals input date prefix" $?

# 6. username/email/id correctness
jq -n --slurpfile u $U --slurpfile r $R '($u[0]|map({key:(.id|tostring),value:.})|from_entries) as $m | all($r[0][]; (. as $x | $m[($x.user_id|tostring)] as $s | $x.username==$s.username and $x.email==$s.email))' | grep -q true; chk "id/username/email mapping correct" $?

# 7. role_count and primary_role correctness (incl. null)
jq -n --slurpfile u $U --slurpfile r $R '($u[0]|map({key:(.id|tostring),value:.})|from_entries) as $m | all($r[0][]; (. as $x | $m[($x.user_id|tostring)] as $s | $x.role_count == ($s.roles|length) and (if ($s.roles|length)==0 then $x.primary_role == null else $x.primary_role == $s.roles[0] end)))' | grep -q true; chk "role_count + primary_role correct (null when empty)" $?

# 8. primary_role is real JSON null (not "null" string) for empty-role users
jq -e 'all(.[]|select(.role_count==0); .primary_role == null)' $R >/dev/null; chk "empty roles -> JSON null" $?
jq -e '[.[]|select(.role_count==0)]|length > 0' $R >/dev/null; chk "there is at least one null-primary_role case exercised" $?

# 9. sorted ascending by username
jq -e '[.[].username] as $n | $n == ($n|sort)' $R >/dev/null; chk "sorted ascending by username" $?

# 10. 2-space indentation, canonical jq formatting
jq --indent 2 . $R | diff -q - $R >/dev/null; chk "file is canonical jq 2-space-indented JSON" $?
grep -q '^  {' $R; chk "indent visibly 2 spaces" $?
SH
sh /tmp/verify.sh
